name: k-th divisor
description: You are given two integers n and k . Find k -th smallest divisor of n , or report that it doesn't exist. Divisor of n is any such natural number, that n can be divided by it without remainder.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers n and k ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 15 , 1 ≤ k ≤ 10 9 ).
output_specification: If n has less than k divisors, output -1 . Otherwise, output the k -th smallest divisor of n .
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 762A — k-th divisor [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
